extracted.intended_audience: petitioners/employers, immigration attorneys, designated school officials (DSOs), beneficiaries (L-1 and M-1), consular and USCIS officers
extracted.subtask_description: U.S. immigration regulatory requirements for L-1 intracompany transferee petitions (individual and blanket), limits, revocation/appeal, admission and extension rules, and M-1 vocational student admission, maintenance, transfers, extensions, and practical training rules. Includes procedural evidentiary and form requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-797 contents for individual petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-797 shall include the beneficiary's name and classification and the petition's period of validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual petition approved under this paragraph shall be valid for the period of established need for the beneficiary's services, not to exceed three years, except where the beneficiary is coming to the United States to open or to be employed in a new office. If beneficiary is coming to open or be employed in a new office, petition may be approved for a period not to exceed one year, after which petitioner must demonstrate it is doing business as defined to extend validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I-797 contents for blanket petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-797 shall identify the approved organizations included in the petition and the petition's period of validity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A blanket petition approved under this paragraph shall be valid initially for a period of three years and may be extended indefinitely thereafter if the qualifying organizations have complied with these regulations. A blanket petition may be approved in whole or in part and shall cover only qualifying organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirement for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file an amended petition, with fee, at the USCIS office where the original petition was filed to reflect changes in approved relationships, additional qualifying organizations under a blanket petition, change in capacity of employment, or any information which would affect the beneficiary's eligibility under section 101(a)(15)(L) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include change from specialized knowledge position to managerial position. Use amended petition to reflect any material info affecting eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spouse and dependents entitlement (L-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The spouse and unmarried minor children of the beneficiary are entitled to L nonimmigrant classification, subject to the same period of admission and limits as the beneficiary, if accompanying or following-to-join the beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither the spouse nor any child may accept employment unless he or she has been granted employment authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial notification timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual or blanket petition is denied, the petitioner shall be notified within 30 days after the date a completed petition has been filed of the denial, the reasons for the denial, and the right to appeal the denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a blanket petition is denied in part, the USCIS office shall forward a Form I-797 listing those organizations which were found to qualify. If denial is reversed on appeal, a new Form I-797 shall be sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority and grounds for revocation of petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: The director may revoke a petition at any time, even after the expiration of the petition. Approval is automatically revoked if petitioner withdraws petition or fails to request indefinite validity of a blanket petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation on notice: director shall send notice of intent to revoke if finds one or more entities no longer qualifying; alien no longer eligible; qualifying org violated requirements; statement of facts untrue; approval involved gross error; or none of qualifying orgs used blanket procedure for three consecutive years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation notice and rebuttal process
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of intent to revoke shall contain a detailed statement of the grounds for the revocation and the time period allowed for the petitioner's rebuttal. Upon receipt, the petitioner may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 days of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The director shall consider all relevant evidence presented in deciding whether to revoke the petition in whole or in part. If a blanket petition is revoked in part, remainder remains approved and a revised Form I-797 shall be sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of beneficiaries upon revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual petition is revoked, the beneficiary shall be required to leave the United States, unless the beneficiary has obtained other work authorization from the Service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a blanket petition is revoked and petitioner and beneficiaries already in US are otherwise eligible for L classification, director shall extend blanket petition for a period necessary to support the stay of those blanket L beneficiaries. Approval notice Form I-171C shall include only names of qualifying orgs and covered beneficiaries. No new beneficiaries may be classified or admitted under this limited extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of denials and revocations
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition denied in whole or in part may be appealed under 8 CFR part 103. A petition revoked on notice in whole or in part may be appealed under part 103. Automatic revocations may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination on Form I-129S is part of petition process and is appealable in same manner as the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission tied to petition validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary may apply for admission to the United States only while the individual or blanket petition is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiary of an individual petition shall not be admitted for a date past validity of petition. Beneficiary of blanket petition may be admitted for three years even though initial validity may expire earlier. Burden on petitioner to file for indefinite validity or file individual petition to support alien's status if blanket will expire while alien in US. Admission period for any alien under 101(a)(15)(L) shall not exceed three years unless extension of stay granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: L-1 cumulative period-of-stay limits
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who has spent five years in the United States in a specialized knowledge capacity or seven years in a managerial or executive capacity under section 101(a)(15)(L) and/or (H) may not be readmitted under L-1 or H unless the alien has resided and been physically present outside the United States for the immediate prior year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such visits do not interrupt the one year abroad, but do not count toward fulfillment. A new individual petition may not be approved for an alien who has spent the maximum time unless the alien resided and was physically present outside the U.S. for the immediate prior year. Petitioner shall provide information about employment, place of residence, and dates and purpose of trips for previous year. Consular or Service officer may not grant L classification under blanket petition to an alien who has spent five/ seven years unless requirements met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to L-1 period limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The five- and seven-year limitations shall not apply to aliens who do not reside continually in the U.S. and whose employment is seasonal, intermittent, or consists of an aggregate of six months or less per year; and to aliens who reside abroad and regularly commute to the U.S. to engage in part-time employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner and alien must provide clear and convincing proof, such as arrival/departure records, tax returns, and records of employment abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary use and retention of Form I-797 and Form I-129S (individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiary of an individual petition who does not require a nonimmigrant visa may present a copy of Form I-797 at a port of entry to facilitate entry into the United States. The copy shall be retained by the beneficiary and presented during the validity of the petition for entry/reentry to resume the same employment and to apply for extension of stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A beneficiary who is required to present a visa and whose visa will expire before intended return may use an original Form I-797 to apply for a new/revalidated visa during petition validity and to apply for extension of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary use and retention of Form I-797 and Form I-129S (blanket)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each alien seeking L classification and admission under a blanket petition shall present a copy of Form I-797 and a Form I-129S from the petitioner identifying position and organization from which employee is transferring, new organization and position, description of duties for both positions, and positions/dates/locations of previous L stays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A current copy of Form I-797 and Form I-129S should be retained by beneficiary and used for leaving/reentering to resume employment with a qualifying organization, applying for new/revalidated visa, and applying for readmission. Alien may be readmitted even though reassigned to a different organization named on Form I-797 than shown on Form I-129S if job duties are virtually the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of visa petition validity — individual
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must file a petition extension on Form I-129 to extend an individual petition under section 101(a)(15)(L) of the Act. A petition extension generally may be filed only if the validity of the original petition has not expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new offices, extension may be by filing new application/petition with evidentiary requirements (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of visa petition validity — new offices evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A visa petition under section 101(a)(15)(L) involving opening a new office may be extended by filing a new application/petition accompanied by evidence that the U.S. and foreign entities are still qualifying organizations; evidence U.S. entity has been doing business for previous year; statement of duties performed previous year and duties under extended petition; statement describing staffing of new operation including number of employees and positions with evidence of wages when beneficiary will be managerial/executive; and evidence of financial status of U.S. operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items document that the new office has become an ongoing business meeting definition requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of blanket petition — procedure and report
rubrics_metrics.description: A blanket petition may only be extended indefinitely by filing a new Form I-129 with a copy of the previous approval notice and a report of admissions during the preceding three years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must include list of aliens admitted under the blanket petition during preceding three years including positions held, employing entity, and dates of initial admission and final departure of each alien. Petitioner shall state whether it still meets criteria for filing a blanket petition and document any changes in approved relationships and additional qualifying organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if blanket petitioner fails to request indefinite validity
rubrics_metrics.description: If petitioner in an approved blanket petition fails to request indefinite validity or if indefinite validity is denied, petitioner and its other qualifying organizations shall seek L classification by filing individual petitions until another three years have expired; after which petitioner may seek approval of a new blanket petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of stay procedure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual petitions, petitioner must apply for petition extension and the alien's extension of stay concurrently on Form I-129. For blanket beneficiaries, a new certificate of eligibility plus copy of previous approved certificate shall be filed to request extension of alien's stay. Beneficiary must be physically present in the U.S. when extension of stay is filed. Director makes separate determinations on petition and extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director may cable notification of approval to consular office abroad if alien required to leave while requests pending. Extensions may be authorized in increments up to two years. Total period of stay may not exceed five years for specialized knowledge beneficiaries and seven years for managerial/executive beneficiaries. No further extensions may be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion-related extension eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: When alien initially admitted in specialized knowledge capacity is later promoted to managerial or executive position, must have been employed in managerial/executive position for at least six months to be eligible for total period of stay of seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change to managerial or executive capacity must have been approved by the Service in an amended, new, or extended petition at the time that the change occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of immigrant filings on L-1 classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing of application for or approval of a permanent labor certification, preference petition, or application for adjustment of status for an L-1 nonimmigrant shall not be the basis for denying an L-1 petition, extension of an L-1 petition, application for admission as an L-1 nonimmigrant, or related change of status/applications enumerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically enumerated items that shall not be denied include (i) an L-1 petition filed on behalf of the alien, (ii) a request to extend an L-1 petition previously filed, (iii) an application for admission as an L-1 or L-2, (iv) application for change of status to H-1 or L-2 by the alien or to other statuses by L-2 spouse/child, (v) change of status to H-4 in certain cases, (vi) application for extension of stay by alien or L-2 spouse/child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedures for Canadian citizens under USMCA (individual)
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. or foreign employer seeking to classify a citizen of Canada as an intracompany transferee may file an individual petition in duplicate on form prescribed by USCIS in conjunction with application for admission at a Class A port of entry located on the U.S.-Canada land border or at a U.S. pre-clearance/pre-flight station in Canada. Petitioning employer need not appear but form must bear authorized signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At these locations an immigration officer may determine eligibility of individual Canadians seeking L classification under approved blanket petitions; Canadians shall present original and two copies of Form I-129S prepared by the approved organization and three copies of Form I-797.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deficient or clearly deniable petitions at port for Canadians
rubrics_metrics.description: If a petition or certificate of eligibility submitted concurrently with an application for admission is lacking necessary supporting documentation or otherwise deficient, the inspecting officer shall return it to the applicant to obtain necessary documentation. Fee to file will be remitted when deficiency is overcome. If clearly deniable, officer will accept petition (with fee) and notify petitioner of denial and right of appeal; if formal denial cannot be issued by port, petition with recommendation for denial forwarded to appropriate Service Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate Service Center is the one within the same Service region as location where application for admission made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial due to labor disputes (Canadians and Mexicans)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Secretary of Labor certifies or informs Commissioner that a strike or labor dispute involving work stoppage is in progress where beneficiary is to be employed and temporary entry may adversely affect settlement or employment of persons involved, a petition to classify a citizen of Mexico or Canada as L-1 may be denied or approval suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not certified or Service not informed, Commissioner shall not deny or suspend. If alien has commenced employment and is participating in a strike/work stoppage, participation alone does not mean failing to maintain status, but status/authorized stay not modified; violation of status or overstaying may lead to deportation.

rubrics_metrics.name: M-1 admission eligibility and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonimmigrant student may be admitted in M nonimmigrant status if the student presents a Form I-20 or successor form issued in the student's own name by a school certified by SEVP for attendance by M-1 foreign students; has documentary evidence of financial support in amount indicated on Form I-20; and for initial admission only, intends to attend the school specified in the student's visa (or if visa-exempt, the school indicated on Form I-20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of SEVIS by schools for M-1 students
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools must issue a Form I-20 or successor form in SEVIS to any current student requiring a reportable action (e.g., extension of stay, practical training, and requests for employment authorization) or a new Form I-20 or successor form, or for any aliens who must obtain a new nonimmigrant student visa.

rubrics_metrics.name: M-1 student maintenance of Form I-20
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student is expected to retain the initial Form I-20 or successor form bearing the admission number and any subsequent Form I-20(s). If student loses current Form I-20, a replacement copy bearing same information including any endorsement for employment and notations should be issued by the DSO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of M-2 spouse and minor children
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouse and minor children accompanying an M-1 student are eligible for admission in M-2 status if the student is admitted in M-1 status. Following-to-join dependents eligible if they can demonstrate the M-1 student has been admitted and is, or will be within 30 days, enrolled in a full course of study or engaged in approved practical training following completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At time they seek admission, each dependent must present a Form I-20 issued in their name by a SEVP-certified school. A new Form I-20 required for a dependent where there has been any substantive change in the M-1 student's current information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary absence — Form I-20 requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student returning from temporary absence to attend the previously authorized school must present either a properly endorsed Form I-20 if no substantive change in student's most recent Form I-20 since initially issued; or a new Form I-20 if there has been any substantive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If student transferred between schools, the name of transfer-in school does not need to be specified in the student's visa.

rubrics_metrics.name: M-1 period of stay calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: A student in M nonimmigrant status is admitted for the period necessary to complete the course of study indicated on the Form I-20 plus practical training following completion, plus an additional 30 days to depart the U.S., but not to exceed a total period of one year. An M-1 student may be admitted up to 30 days before the report or start date listed on Form I-20. An M-1 student who fails to maintain a full course of study or otherwise fails to maintain status is not eligible for the additional 30-day period of stay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of full course of study for M-1 students
rubrics_metrics.description: Full course of study must lead to attainment of a specific educational/vocational objective and be at an institution certified for attendance by foreign students. Definitions: (i) community/junior college—at least 12 semester/quarter hours per term (or equivalent); (ii) postsecondary vocational/business school—confers recognized associate or other degrees or credits accepted unconditionally by at least three other institutions and certified to consist of at least 12 clock hours per week (or equivalent); (iii) vocational/nonacademic curriculum—at least 18 clock hours/week if classroom dominant, or 22 clock hours/week if shop/lab dominant; (iv) vocational/high school curriculum—class attendance for not less than minimum hours prescribed for normal progress toward graduation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On-line/distance education: no online/distance education classes may be considered to count toward M-1 full course requirement if such classes do not require student's physical attendance for classes, examination or other purposes integral to completion. Defines online/distance course examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduced course load for M-1 students
rubrics_metrics.description: DSO may authorize less than a full course of study only where student has been compelled by illness or a medical condition documented by a licensed medical doctor, doctor of osteopathy, licensed psychologist, or licensed clinical psychologist to interrupt or reduce course of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A DSO may not authorize reduced course load for more than an aggregate of 5 months per course of study. A student previously authorized to drop below full course due to illness/medical condition for 5 months may not be authorized to reduce load on subsequent occasions during their particular course of study. DSO must update SEVIS prior to student reducing load.

rubrics_metrics.name: M-1 extension of stay eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative time of extensions that can be granted to an M-1 student is limited to a period of 3 years from original start date, plus 30 days. No extension if student unable to complete course within 3 years of original program start date. Extension may be granted if bona fide nonimmigrant currently maintaining status; compelling educational or medical reasons caused delay (academic probation/suspension not acceptable); and student able and in good faith intends to continue to maintain status for period of extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must be on Form I-539, including M-2 spouse/children if applicable, submitted at least 15 but not more than 60 days before program end date, accompanied by Form I-20 and Form I-94 if applicable. If granted, extension period equals time necessary to complete course plus 30 days or total period of one year, whichever is less. M-2 dependents not eligible for extension unless M-1 granted. Form I-20 must be endorsed with recommendation and new program end date for submission and SEVIS updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: M-1 school transfer eligibility and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student may not transfer to another school after six months from date first admitted as, or changes status to, M-1 unless student unable to remain at initial school due to circumstances beyond student's control. Student may be otherwise eligible to transfer if bona fide nonimmigrant, has been pursuing full course at last authorized school, intends to pursue full course at transfer-in school, and is financially able to attend transfer-in school.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfer procedure: apply to USCIS on Form I-539 for permission; transfer subject to approval. Student must notify transfer-out school, which updates SEVIS and inputs transfer release date. Transfer-in school generates Form I-20 but will not gain access to SEVIS record until release date. Upon receipt of Form I-20 from transfer-in school, student must submit Form I-539. Student may enroll in next available term and must notify DSO of transfer-in school upon beginning attendance. Transfer-in school must update SEVIS. Upon approval USCIS will transmit approval to SEVIS. If transfer denied, student is out of status and record must be terminated in SEVIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement requirement for students not pursuing full course
rubrics_metrics.description: If an M-1 student who has not been pursuing a full course of study desires to attend a different school, the student must apply for reinstatement to student status under paragraph (m)(16) of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on change in educational objective for M-1
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student may not change educational objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment prohibition for M-1 students
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (m)(14) (practical training), a student may not accept employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: M-1 practical training authorization conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary employment for practical training may be authorized only after completion of the student's course of study if: (A) proposed employment is recommended for the purpose of practical training; (B) proposed employment is related to the student's course of study; and (C) upon DSO's information and belief, employment comparable to proposed employment is not available to student in country of foreign residence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application: student must apply on Form I-765 with fee, accompanied by properly endorsed Form I-20 by DSO for practical training. Application must be submitted before program end date but not more than 90 days before program end date. DSO must certify on Form I-538 the three conditions above. Duration: when authorized to engage in employment for practical training, student will be issued an EAD.
